x: The result of the Club handicap held by courtesy of Ashcombe A.C., in connection with their meeting on July 26th, resulted as follows :— 1, A.

As the National Junior Race will be over before this issue is out, little need be said, but young Mac's present form is good enough to annexe the individual title and that he will receive good support from Bert East, Harry Rouse, Joe Wilson and others.
Young McMullen, walking comfortably throughout, finished nearly a minute in front of Bert East, with Joe Wilson third. The handicap was won by Don Heath with Sid Spencer second and Joe Wilson third.
That incredible old-timer Bert East is still walking better than ever and improving with every race. His latest effort is to beat Rutland, McMullen and Coleman in the Club 10.

Added to all these sterling performances he won the Club Championship in a new Championship time of 14.11.2 and the Inter Counties 7 miles Championship at White City on August Monday. In the veteran class Bert East appears to have been quite prominent. On 31st July, he finished third in a Veterans A.C.
The race this year was held at Bradford and at about 7½ miles, after it looked as though we were in a fairly comfortable position, Bert East failed to please the judges and was ruled out.

A field of 22 juniors lined up for the start and once again Bert East led them home, with George Bentley second and Pat Sapcote third. Charlie Speechley, still having a go, won the Handicap, with George Atkinson second and Joe Scammell third.
A number of our walkers have figured well in Open Handicaps and Veterans' Events, successes being scored by Bert East, Syd James, Charlie Speechley and young Joe Scamell.
Twenty-two of our members, including " Sir " Harry Shields, lined up for the Horwood Cup Race when Bert East, maintaining his remarkable form, soon went into the lead.
A.

To describe the race briefly, we had a very early shock when Bert East was disqualified in the first half mile. Although this must have dismayed the first four Belgrave lads who seemed to be the only team men to know of this upheaval of our plans, they set to straight away to endeavour to make up the loss.
Owing to many other fixtures we were not very strong and although Bert East was first home, the match resulted in a win for Walton A.C., 17 pts; S.W.C., 2nd, 29 pts.; and Belgrave, 3rd, 32 pts.

A bare team of four started in this event, the only open race held on a Sunday, and Bert East walked well to finish third. Charlie Speechley, making one of his rare appearances, was our fourth scoring man and the team finished 4th in the scratch race.

Joe Scamell won a Veterans' mile handicap at Parliament Hill Fields on August 23rd off 22 yards. Bert East won the Veterans' A.C. 2 miles Championship and was second in the Erith Open Mile on August 7th.

We feel that Harry was definitely unlucky in being so ruled and with Bert East also suffering disqualification in the last half-mile of the race our team was too depleted to be a danger, and we feel that we did very well to finish third in the scratch team race.
Syd James, showing a welcome return to form, showed a clean pair of heels to the opposition after the first two miles and walked faultlessly to finish in 39.45, with Bert East second.

Once again we have to report the disqualification of Harry Churcher, who up to five and a half miles had walked splendidly and fairly, and with Mac and Syd James well up, with Bert East and George Oliver lying handy, we had visions of a team win, which, in spite of Harry's misfortune, eventually materialised.

Eric Hall continued with his run of successes with an easy win in the 2 miles walk for which, incidentally, there were only four competitors; of which Bert East was one - surely our walkers could support this event in greater strength.
Bert East and Logan had a dust up for 173rd position followed by our second claim member Tubby Gittins. Sheffield proved themselves once again unbeatable.

Russell 27th, Nick Milsum 28th, Wally Emery 29th and veteran Bert East 34th, totalling 11 of the 39 finishers. Stan Vickers off 2mins. was 2nd in the handicap with Ray Switzer (7.30) 3rd, so we took a good share of the prizes.

Froude and D, Stevens gave a forward display and our two veterans Charlie Speechley and Bert East battled bravely through to the end. In the Surrey Championship we once again secured double honours, Harry Churcher leading the team in his usual style, followed by Charlie, Mac (Dave McMullen) and Bert East.
The Belgrave Open 5 miles handicap held at Battersea Park on July 2nd was finally won by M.Oliver of Enfield despite Bert East fighting to the end.
Amongst those of his contemporaries he was asking after BERT EAST - he was pleasantly surprised to be directed to a corner where Bert was preparing himself for another Open Seven.

Bert East, who we are sure will not mind us revealing that he is now 73, regularly competes in walking races but just recently taught himself to swim and can now cover three or four widths of the baths.
